title: The Sam Morgan band: repertoire and members
summary: Howard recalls the Morgan band's repertoire, Sam's sweet trumpet style, and members including Yank, Alfred Williams, Roy Evans and the Jims.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What kind of a band? They made some records. I mean, when you played with them, what type of music did they play? They made some records of some spirituals for one thing. Yeah. Well, I was playing trumpet when they made that. I was in that place. I had my own band. You see? I just wondered, when you were a member, what type of music they played?
Well, they played the Red Book numbers and they had some pretty good musicians there. Yank was playing trombone. Well, full shade. Some of the rag down numbers too.

Yeah, they played, yeah. I wondered because the first time you made your records you played the Climax Rag, which I've never heard of you before. Yeah. You seem to know all those old numbers. I know, man. Some of those with the Morgan Band things.
Yeah, well, yeah, but Morgan Band, well, Sam never, how they played the rough trumpet, he was on the sweet side.

He was on the sweet side. Yeah, he was sweet, straight, and he was on the right. Straight, sweet. Did they have an unusually good beat? A lot of people thought it was a wonderful dance band. It was a wonderful dance band.

Alfred Williams, you know Alfred Williams, he was the drummer. Rudolph was the drummer. And Roy, Roy Evans, he's dead long while. Well, he had some good men. Little Jim was like I told you, he was playing bass. Then after, Big Jim played, but Yank, he played at that time.
How does Yank play? I never know anything about him, never hear much of anybody mentioning him hard of that.

Well, Yank was a good trombone player. He was no high played man. You know what I mean, you know, way up there, but except right in that tradition, he could read too. So Yank played, and his brother played trombone too.
